subtitle: Natale a Toronto
intro: December 22nd, Pearson again: this time Chiara holds the sign. {hero} is home for ten days with a southern accent and stories of Roccamarina; the two cousins compare lives in the basement kitchen while Franco reports what everyone said at the Vigilia. Crossover with [[IT Unit 19]] and [[IT Unit 24]]. This unit builds the English [[reported speech]] in full with the backshift of tenses, the two patterns of [[say]] vs [[tell]], and the Italo-Canadian Christmas vocabulary.
objectives: Riportare quello che qualcuno ha detto, chiesto o ordinato: [[she said she was tired]], [[he told me to call]], [[they asked if we had eaten]]
Backshift completo: [[I am]] → [[she said she was]], [[I saw]] → [[she said she'd seen]], [[I will]] → [[she said she would]]
Spostare tempo e luogo: [[here]] → [[there]], [[tomorrow]] → [[the next day]], [[this]] → [[that]], [[now]] → [[then]]
Distinguere say e tell: [[she said that…]] vs [[she told me that…]]
canDo: B1 · Spoken production: can report accurately what someone said, asked or requested.
B1 · Spoken interaction: can relay news between two people and respond to follow-up questions.
B1 · Reading: can follow a long chat thread, a news report or an interview with reported speech.
B1 · Writing: can summarise a conversation or report a letter for a third party.
B1 · Lexis: can describe Canadian and Italo-Canadian Christmas customs.

sections.title: Pearson again, and the Vigilia
sections.intro: The three scenes of a Toronto Christmas: the airport pickup with Chiara holding the sign; dinner at the Ferrantes' on the Vigilia with seven dishes of fish; a basement-kitchen compare-lives conversation after midnight. Listen for reported speech (she said, she told me), tense backshift, and the Italo-Canadian menu.

blocks.title: December 22, 4:30 p.m., Terminal 1
blocks.setting: Pearson International Airport, Terminal 1, Arrivals Hall D. Chiara with a hand-drawn sign that reads WELCOME HOME COUSIN. Twenty centimetres of snow outside; -8°C with the wind chill. {hero} coming through the sliding doors with one bag.

lines.t: {hero}! Over here! You're last off. Franco said the plane had landed at 3:50, but then they held you for passport control for forty minutes. Welcome. Give me a hug.
lines.n: {hero}! Qui! Sei l'ultimo a uscire. Franco ha detto che l'aereo era atterrato alle 15:50, ma poi ti hanno trattenuto al controllo passaporti per quaranta minuti. Benvenuto. Dammi un abbraccio.
lines.note: Franco said the plane had landed: reported past-of-past. He said → the plane HAD landed (further back). Standard backshift.

lines.t: I'm here. — Did you grow? — You've got a Canadian accent. — I don't have an accent. I have a southern Italian accent you now hear as different. — Pasquale told me yesterday that I should bring his regards; Dora told me three times to make sure you had Chiara's cold medicine; Nando asked how much the taxi from the airport costs here.
lines.n: Sono qui. — Sei cresciuta? — Hai l'accento canadese. — Non ho un accento. Ho l'accento meridionale che adesso senti diverso. — Pasquale mi ha detto ieri di portargli i saluti; Dora mi ha detto tre volte di assicurarmi che tu avessi la medicina per il raffreddore; Nando ha chiesto quanto costa il taxi dall'aeroporto qui.
lines.note: Pasquale told me to bring: reported request (told + object + to + inf). Dora told me to make sure you had: layered — reported order + reported statement. Nando asked how much: reported wh-question.

lines.t: Taxi from here is 70 to 90 dollars. Transit is 11, but it takes an hour and a half. Franco said he would come with the van. He texted twenty minutes ago that he was in short-term parking and that we should take our time. — Did Dora really tell you three times?
lines.n: Il taxi da qui è 70-90 dollari. I mezzi 11, ma ci vuole un'ora e mezza. Franco ha detto che sarebbe venuto con il furgone. Mi ha scritto venti minuti fa che era in short-term parking e che ci saremmo presi tutto il tempo. — Dora te l'ha detto davvero tre volte?
lines.note: Franco said he would come: future-in-the-past. He texted that he was in parking: reported statement with backshift. We should take our time: reported suggestion.

lines.t: Four times. The first time said «give it to her the day she arrives»; the second said «give it to her the day after her shift»; the third said «for God's sake don't forget it»; the fourth said «did you remember?».
lines.n: Quattro. La prima volta ha detto «gliela devi dare il giorno in cui arriva»; la seconda «gliela devi dare il giorno dopo il turno»; la terza «per l'amor del cielo non te la dimenticare»; la quarta «te la sei ricordata?».
lines.note: Four reported commands in rising intensity. The direct speech vs reported-order patterns.

lines.t: That is Dora, exactly. — Franco! Over here! The protagonist is here. — Benvenuti. Pasta's ready at Teresa's at six, so we have to move. The 401 is going to be slow with the snow.
lines.n: Questa è Dora, esattamente. — Franco! Qui! Il protagonista è arrivato. — Benvenuti. La pasta da Teresa è pronta alle sei, quindi dobbiamo muoverci. La 401 sarà lenta con la neve.
lines.note: Franco switches to Italian for the welcome, then back to English for the practical part. Standard code-switching.

lines.t: Did I tell you? Your zia Teresa cooked for forty people. Priya's coming, Doug and his wife are coming, Mateo is coming, Sofia's roommate Linh is coming. Teresa said she wasn't going to let anyone eat alone on the Vigilia. — You look just like your mother at twenty-six.
lines.n: Te l'ho detto? Tua zia Teresa ha cucinato per quaranta persone. Priya viene, Doug e la moglie, Mateo, la coinquilina di Sofia Linh. Teresa ha detto che non avrebbe lasciato mangiare nessuno da solo alla Vigilia. — Sei identica a tua madre a ventisei anni.
lines.note: Teresa said she wasn't going to let anyone eat: reported future-in-the-past with going to → was going to. You look just like your mother: a compliment often heard across diasporas.

notes.phrase: Franco said the plane had landed · Pasquale told me to bring · Dora told me to make sure · Nando asked how much the taxi costs · Franco said he would come
notes.note: Five reported-speech moves. Said + that (optional) + backshifted clause; told + object + to + infinitive for an order.

notes.phrase: Toronto 70–90 dollar taxi · 401 slow with the snow · Vigilia at 6 · forty people cooked for · twenty centimetres of snow · -8°C with the wind chill
notes.note: The specifics of an Italo-Canadian Christmas in Toronto: the air, the drive, the house.

blocks.title: La Vigilia · seven fish, forty people
blocks.setting: December 24, 7 p.m. Franco and Teresa's house, Vaughan. Table set for twenty-two in the dining room, the Christmas tree in the corner, candles lit, Vince Gill on the stereo. The seven fish arrive in sequence; the kitchen is already working on the dolci.
blocks.register: informal multigenerational family, English with Italian insertions

lines.t: Everyone to the table. Chiara, next to your cousin; {hero}, next to Chiara; Franco at the head. The old Ferrante rule is: the Vigilia is seven fish — baccalà, calamari, sarde, scampi, insalata di mare, pasta con le vongole, and the big one. Don't ask me what the seventh is. It's a surprise.
lines.n: Tutti a tavola. Chiara, accanto a tuo cugino; {hero}, accanto a Chiara; Franco a capotavola. La vecchia regola Ferrante è: la Vigilia è sette pesci — baccalà, calamari, sarde, scampi, insalata di mare, pasta con le vongole, e il grande. Non mi chiedere qual è il settimo. È una sorpresa.
lines.note: Seven dishes of fish on Christmas Eve — the Feast of the Seven Fishes, actually an Italo-American invention that became Italo-Canadian too. In Italy the Vigilia is one fish dish, usually baccalà.

lines.t: I'm vegetarian. — I know, I made a baccalà in bianco con the sauce on the side and a pasta with the clam sauce separate. For you I made a melanzane parmigiana. I didn't want you to feel left out. — I wasn't going to say anything, but thank you.
lines.n: Sono vegetariana. — Lo so, ho fatto un baccalà in bianco con la salsa a parte e una pasta con il sugo di vongole a parte. Per te ho fatto una parmigiana di melanzane. Non volevo che ti sentissi tagliata fuori. — Non avrei detto niente, ma grazie.
lines.note: I wasn't going to say anything, but thank you: the past of be going to for an unfulfilled intention. Teresa's hospitality is the engine of this scene.

lines.t: {hero}, Chiara explained to me last week that you'd stayed open through the holidays last year. She said that the shop had taken the first real money in September, that Tommaso had thought he was going to leave, and that one Monday Pasquale came in and the rest you know. Is that right?
lines.n: {hero}, Chiara mi ha spiegato la settimana scorsa che eri rimasto aperto per le feste l'anno scorso. Ha detto che l'officina aveva incassato il primo denaro vero a settembre, che Tommaso aveva pensato di andarsene, e che un lunedì è arrivato Pasquale e il resto lo sai. È così?
lines.note: Chiara explained that you'd stayed open: reported statement, past perfect for a prior past. She said that the shop had taken: backshift. Three past perfects stacked in Franco's report.

lines.t: Mostly. Pasquale will tell you it was the «caffè» that saved it. I'd tell you it was that Dora had already called her cousin at the bank, and that Tommaso had rejected the other offer the week before, and that Nando had a loan ready that I never used. Everyone had done something.
lines.n: Più o meno. Pasquale ti direbbe che è stato il «caffè» a salvarla. Io ti direi che era che Dora aveva già chiamato il cugino in banca, e che Tommaso aveva rifiutato l'altra offerta la settimana prima, e che Nando aveva pronto un prestito che non ho mai usato. Ognuno aveva fatto qualcosa.
lines.note: Pasquale will tell you (future, direct) vs I'd tell you (conditional, hypothetical). Four past perfects in a row for the layered prior actions.

lines.t: Dora reminded me on the phone yesterday that she had always told {hero} that the shop would make it. She said she'd been sure «from the first week», which, come on. She also said she'd known Nando had a loan ready — I don't think she did. She just claims these things.
lines.n: Dora mi ha ricordato ieri al telefono che aveva sempre detto a {hero} che l'officina ce l'avrebbe fatta. Ha detto di essere stata sicura «dalla prima settimana», il che, dai. Ha anche detto che aveva saputo che Nando aveva pronto un prestito — non credo che lo sapesse. Lo rivendica.
lines.note: Dora reminded me that she had always told: reported statement with double past perfect. She said she'd been sure: past perfect. She said she'd known: past perfect. The reported-speech choreography of a family rumour.

lines.t: This is my first Vigilia. In Mexico we have Nochebuena, December 24, with tamales and ponche and the baby Jesus in the manger at midnight. I'd been told that Italian Christmas was all food, but I didn't realise it was seven courses before the main meal.
lines.n: Questa è la mia prima Vigilia. In Messico abbiamo la Nochebuena, il 24 dicembre, con tamales e ponche e il Gesù bambino nella mangiatoia a mezzanotte. Mi avevano detto che il Natale italiano era tutto cibo, ma non immaginavo che fossero sette portate prima del piatto principale.
lines.note: I'd been told that Italian Christmas was all food: reported passive (I had been told) with backshift. Spot the layered perfect.

lines.t: Mateo, we are only halfway. The baccalà is the appetiser. The pasta con le vongole is the primo. The scampi is the secondo. The big one is coming. — Teresa, is tonight the night we tell them what the seventh fish is? — Not yet. After the panettone.
lines.n: Mateo, siamo solo a metà. Il baccalà è l'antipasto. La pasta alle vongole è il primo. Gli scampi sono il secondo. Il grande sta arrivando. — Teresa, è la sera in cui diciamo loro qual è il settimo pesce? — Non ancora. Dopo il panettone.
lines.note: The structure of an Italo-Canadian Christmas Eve: appetiser, pasta, fish, big fish, dolci and the seventh fish as a running family joke.

notes.phrase: Chiara explained that you'd stayed open · she said the shop had taken · Dora reminded me she had always told · I'd been told that · Teresa said she wasn't going to let anyone eat alone
notes.note: Five reported-speech moves: say, tell (with and without object), remind (+ that), passive be told. Backshift from past simple to past perfect, from past perfect to past perfect (no shift), from going to to was going to.

notes.phrase: baccalà · calamari · sarde · scampi · insalata di mare · pasta con le vongole · panettone · pandoro · Vigilia · the seven fish
notes.note: The Italo-Canadian Christmas menu. The Feast of the Seven Fishes is an Italo-American tradition that spread to Italo-Canadian households; in Italy the Vigilia is usually one fish.

blocks.title: After midnight · basement kitchen
blocks.setting: December 25, 1:30 a.m. The Ferrantes' basement kitchen. Chiara and {hero} with the leftovers. The two cousins compare lives.

lines.t: I was going to say to you earlier, when the uncles were talking, that I like it here. I didn't say it then because I didn't want to upset Dora if someone videoed it. — You can say it now.
lines.n: Volevo dirti prima, mentre gli zii parlavano, che qui mi piace. Non l'ho detto allora perché non volevo turbare Dora se qualcuno avesse ripreso. — Lo puoi dire adesso.
lines.note: I was going to say that I like it here: a reported future-in-the-past intention. If someone videoed it: past subjunctive after if.

lines.t: I like it here too, for ten days. Chiara, Pasquale said to tell you something quietly. He said that the shop was still here because of your «caffè», that the pasticciotti ovens had opened an extra tray every Saturday since you left, and that if you decided to open a bakery in Toronto he would come and clean the floor.
lines.n: Mi piace anche a me, per dieci giorni. Chiara, Pasquale mi ha detto di dirti una cosa a voce bassa. Ha detto che l'officina è ancora qui per il tuo «caffè», che i forni dei pasticciotti hanno aperto un vassoio in più ogni sabato da quando sei partita, e che se decidessi di aprire una pasticceria a Toronto lui verrebbe a pulire il pavimento.
lines.note: Pasquale said to tell you something: say + to + infinitive is rarer than tell + object; here it works for the two-step order. He said that the shop was still here: backshift presente → imperfetto. If you decided to open: a second conditional, inside reported speech.

lines.t: Did he really say that? About the floor? — His exact words were «io stesso». You know Pasquale. He said he had always known I'd do «something strange», that his mother had told him in 1958 that his cousin's daughter would open «la bottega del pane» abroad, and that we were living out an old family story.
lines.n: L'ha detto davvero? Del pavimento? — Le sue parole esatte erano «io stesso». Lo conosci Pasquale. Ha detto che aveva sempre saputo che io avrei fatto «qualcosa di strano», che sua madre gli aveva detto nel 1958 che la figlia della cugina avrebbe aperto «la bottega del pane» all'estero, e che stavamo vivendo una vecchia storia di famiglia.
lines.note: He said he had always known I'd do: past perfect + conditional (future-in-the-past). His mother had told him in 1958 that his cousin's daughter would open: a telescopic reporting layer, three generations deep.

lines.t: The strangest part is that I thought I'd miss Roccamarina more. I don't. I miss Dora. I miss our table. I miss the sea at seven in the morning. But I don't miss the town itself. Does that make me a bad person?
lines.n: La parte più strana è che pensavo che mi sarebbe mancata di più Roccamarina. Non mi manca. Mi manca Dora. Mi manca la nostra tavola. Mi manca il mare alle sette del mattino. Ma il paese in sé no. Mi rende una brutta persona?
lines.note: I thought I'd miss Roccamarina: reported future-in-the-past (I thought I would miss). I don't vs I miss Dora: present-simple contrasts for permanent current state.

lines.t: No. It makes you honest. — I was going to say to you something too. I think I'm going to stay longer than a year. Just so you know, if you decide to apply for permanent residency, I'd come and help with the paperwork.
lines.n: No. Ti rende sincera. — Volevo dirti anch'io una cosa. Credo che mi fermerò più di un anno. Giusto perché tu lo sappia, se decidessi di fare domanda per la residenza permanente, verrei ad aiutarti con i moduli.
lines.note: I was going to say: unfulfilled intention. If you decide to apply, I'd come: second conditional. The two cousins hand each other the next chapter.

notes.phrase: I was going to say · Franco said he would come · Teresa said she wasn't going to let · Pasquale said that the shop was still here · he said he had always known
notes.note: The future-in-the-past constructions: was going to + base (unfulfilled intention); would + base (planned action); had already + past perfect (previous expectation). Compare: Italian condizionale passato in reported speech (unit 19 Italian).

questions.q: «Franco said the plane had landed at 3:50» — the plane landed:
options: Before Franco said that. (prior action in a past narrative)
After Franco said that.
At the same time.
questions.why: Had landed is the past perfect — a prior event in the past.

questions.q: In «Pasquale told me to bring his regards», tell + object + to + infinitive is a reported order (unit 17).
questions.why: Right — tell + object + to + inf = reported order / request. Same pattern as unit 17.

questions.q: «I'm tired» → She said she ___ (be) tired. «I'll come» → She said she ___ (come). «I saw the doctor» → She said she ___ (see) the doctor.
questions.n: «Sono stanca» → Ha detto che era stanca. «Vengo» → Ha detto che sarebbe venuta. «Ho visto il dottore» → Ha detto che aveva visto il dottore.

sections.title: Christmas, reporting verbs, family-at-the-table
sections.intro: Four themes: Christmas vocabulary with Italo-Canadian specifics, the reporting verbs beyond say and tell, the small lexicon of family and gossip, and news vocabulary.

ex.t: Merry Christmas! Happy Holidays!
ex.n: Buon Natale! Buone feste!

items.note: Christmas Day (25); Christmas Eve = la Vigilia (24). Happy Holidays is inclusive of other faiths.

ex.t: Christmas Eve is the big dinner in Italian households.
ex.n: La Vigilia è la grande cena nelle famiglie italiane.

items.note: Also New Year's Eve = la Vigilia di Capodanno = December 31.

ex.t: Boxing Day: the day after Christmas, when the sales start.
ex.n: Boxing Day: il giorno dopo Natale, quando iniziano i saldi.

items.note: A British holiday that stayed in Canada. Big shopping day.

ex.t: New Year's Eve: fireworks and parties. New Year's Day: hangover.
ex.n: La Vigilia: fuochi e feste. Capodanno: dopo-sbornia.

items.note: December 31 / January 1.

ex.t: Christmas is a statutory holiday. We have the day off.
ex.n: Natale è una festa civile. Abbiamo il giorno libero.

items.note: Also British holiday = vacation (US). Statutory holiday / stat: giorno festivo nazionale.

ex.t: We put up the Christmas tree on December 1st.
ex.n: Mettiamo su l'albero di Natale il 1° dicembre.

items.note: Christmas tree. Real tree vs artificial tree.

ex.t: Open gifts on Christmas Day in Canada, not the Vigilia.
ex.n: In Canada i regali si aprono a Natale, non la Vigilia.

items.note: Gift and present are interchangeable. Gift tag: cartellino. Gift receipt: scontrino regalo.

ex.t: Hang your stocking on the mantel on Christmas Eve.
ex.n: Appendi la calza sopra il camino alla Vigilia.

items.note: Different from the Italian Befana. Here, Santa fills the stocking.

ex.t: Santa Claus Parade is in November in Toronto.
ex.n: La parata di Babbo Natale è a novembre a Toronto.

items.note: Santa in short. Father Christmas is more British.

ex.t: Panettone comes from Milan, pandoro from Verona.
ex.n: Il panettone è di Milano, il pandoro di Verona.

items.note: Italian Christmas cakes, now sold everywhere in Toronto. Order from an Italian bakery.

blocks.theme: The seven fish and the Italo-Canadian Christmas
blocks.n: I sette pesci e il Natale italo-canadese

items.t: the Feast of the Seven Fishes

ex.t: The Feast of the Seven Fishes is an Italo-American tradition.
ex.n: La Festa dei Sette Pesci è una tradizione italo-americana.

items.note: Started in the Italian-American diaspora in the early 20th century; adopted by Italo-Canadians. In Italy, the Vigilia is usually one fish dish.

ex.t: Baccalà is salt cod, soaked for 48 hours before cooking.
ex.n: Il baccalà è merluzzo salato, in ammollo 48 ore prima di cuocere.

items.note: The emblematic Vigilia fish. Baccalà vs stoccafisso: salted vs dried.

ex.t: Scampi, calamari and sarde: the classic three.
ex.n: Scampi, calamari e sarde: i tre classici.

items.note: Loan-words kept in English in Italo-Canadian homes.

ex.t: Insalata di mare: squid, octopus, shrimp, lemon.
ex.n: Insalata di mare: calamari, polpo, gamberi, limone.

items.note: Served cold. One of the seven fishes.

ex.t: Linguine with clams: a Christmas Eve staple.
ex.n: Linguine con le vongole: un classico della Vigilia.

items.note: Clams in English. Mussels = cozze.

ex.t: The devout go to midnight mass; everyone else goes to bed.
ex.n: I più devoti vanno alla messa di mezzanotte; gli altri vanno a letto.

items.note: In Italian Catholicism, the midnight mass closes the Vigilia.

ex.t: The manger: the baby Jesus arrives at midnight on the 24th.
ex.n: Il presepe: il bambino Gesù arriva a mezzanotte del 24.

items.note: Also crèche (French-Canadian). The Italian tradition is strong.

ex.t: La Befana comes on January 6th with coal for the bad kids.
ex.n: La Befana arriva il 6 gennaio con il carbone per i cattivi.

items.note: Italian only; not Canadian. The Epiphany witch who brings sweets.

ex.t: Lunar New Year is a big deal in Toronto's Chinatowns.
ex.n: Il Capodanno lunare è importante nelle Chinatowns di Toronto.

items.note: In the Toronto mosaic, parallel to Christmas.

ex.t: Hanukkah is the Jewish festival of lights; Diwali the Hindu one.
ex.n: Hanukkah è la festa delle luci ebraica; Diwali quella induista.

items.note: Both close to Christmas in time and in multicultural practice.

blocks.n: Verbi di riporto oltre say e tell

ex.t: Chiara explained to me that you had stayed open.
ex.n: Chiara mi ha spiegato che eri rimasto aperto.

items.note: Explain + to + object (I explained to her, not I explained her). Explain + that + clause.

ex.t: Priya suggested that we eat the baccalà first.
ex.n: Priya ha proposto di mangiare prima il baccalà.

items.note: Suggest + that + clause (optional subjunctive-looking should: that we eat / that we should eat). Not suggest me (I suggested to her…).

ex.t: She promised she would come back.
ex.n: Ha promesso che sarebbe tornata.

items.note: Promise + to + inf (I promise to call) OR promise + that + clause.

ex.t: She warned me not to try the oven trick.
ex.n: Mi ha avvertita di non provare il trucco del forno.

items.note: Warn + object + to + inf, or + that + clause.

ex.t: She admitted that she had been scared.
ex.n: Ha ammesso che era stata spaventata.

items.note: Admit + that or + -ing (admit lying). Not admit to tell.

ex.t: He complained that the taxi was too expensive.
ex.n: Si è lamentato che il taxi era troppo caro.

items.note: Complain + that + clause OR complain about + noun.

ex.t: Dora reminded me on the phone that she had always told you.
ex.n: Dora mi ha ricordato al telefono che te l'aveva sempre detto.

items.note: Remind + object + that + clause (reminded me that…). Remind + object + to + inf (reminded me to call = ricordato di chiamare).

ex.t: I confess I'd never seen snow before December.
ex.n: Confesso di non aver mai visto la neve prima di dicembre.

items.note: Confess + that or + to + -ing. More formal than admit.

ex.t: He denied that he had made the call.
ex.n: Ha negato di aver fatto la chiamata.

items.note: Deny + that OR deny + -ing (he denied making the call).

ex.t: Teresa insisted that I take a second helping.
ex.n: Teresa ha insistito che prendessi una seconda porzione.

items.note: Insist + that + clause (classic trigger for the surviving-English subjunctive: insist that she go).

ex.t: Half the room is a relative of some kind.
ex.n: Metà della stanza è parente in qualche modo.

items.note: Also family member. Close relative / distant relative.

ex.t: First cousin: parents are siblings. Second cousin: grandparents are siblings.
ex.n: Primo cugino: i genitori sono fratelli. Secondo cugino: i nonni sono fratelli.

items.note: The whole {hero}-Chiara relationship is first cousin.

ex.t: I have two siblings: a brother and a sister.
ex.n: Ho due fratelli: un fratello e una sorella.

items.note: The gender-neutral word for brothers / sisters. Common in official English.

ex.t: The in-laws came for Christmas lunch.
ex.n: I suoceri sono venuti per il pranzo di Natale.

items.note: Mother-in-law, father-in-law, brother-in-law, sister-in-law. In Italian: suocera, suocero, cognato, cognata.

ex.t: The news from Roccamarina: Dora is sleeping again.
ex.n: Le notizie da Roccamarina: Dora dorme di nuovo.

items.note: Uncountable in English: the news is good. Not «a news».

ex.t: Family gossip is better than TV.
ex.n: I pettegolezzi di famiglia sono meglio della TV.

items.note: Also verb: to gossip. Uncountable.

ex.t: There was a rumour Franco was selling the garage.
ex.n: C'era voce che Franco stesse vendendo l'officina.

items.note: Canadian spelling: rumour (British). US: rumor.

ex.t: Give me an update after lunch.
ex.n: Dammi un aggiornamento dopo pranzo.

items.note: Also verb. Casual: what's the latest?

ex.t: We have a lot to catch up on.
ex.n: Abbiamo molto di cui aggiornarci.

items.note: Catch up on + topic. Also catch up with = incontrarsi.

ex.t: Chiara filled me in on the bakery news.
ex.n: Chiara mi ha messo al corrente delle novità della pasticceria.

items.note: Fill (someone) in on (something).

sections.title: Reported speech in full
sections.intro: Three pieces: the full tense backshift of reported speech, the say / tell distinction (unit 17 reports to you, now in full), and the small irregulars (reporting verbs with specific patterns).

blocks.title: Reported speech: backshift
blocks.rule: English reported speech shifts tenses one step into the past when the main verb is in the past (said, told, asked, explained). Present simple → past simple («I'm tired» → she said she was tired). Present continuous → past continuous («I'm cooking» → he said he was cooking). Present perfect → past perfect («I've seen it» → she said she had seen it). Past simple → past perfect (often) OR stays («I saw it» → she said she had seen it / she said she saw it). Past perfect → stays («I had seen it» → she said she had seen it). Will → would («I'll come» → she said she would come). Going to → was/were going to («I'm going to leave» → she said she was going to leave). Can → could, may → might, must → had to or must. Could, would, should, might, ought to usually stay. If the main verb is in the present (she says), no backshift. If the fact is still true (she said the Earth is round), no backshift. Place / time shifts: here → there; now → then; today → that day; tomorrow → the next day / the following day; yesterday → the day before / the previous day; this → that; these → those; last week → the week before.

blocks.title: Say vs tell
blocks.rule: Two patterns to keep separate. Say: no indirect object. Say (something) [to someone]: she said that she was tired; she said hello (to me). Not she said me. Tell: with indirect object. Tell someone (something): he told me that he was leaving; she told the children a story. Tell + object + to + infinitive = order (unit 17): she told me to leave. Say to someone + direct speech: she said to me, «Call me». Fixed phrases with tell (no that): tell a story, tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a joke, tell the difference, tell the time, tell someone's fortune. Fixed phrases with say: say hello / goodbye / sorry / thanks / grace. Reporting verbs grouped by pattern. Say-type (no object before that): say, mention, admit, declare, remark, promise, agree, decide. Tell-type (object before that): tell, inform, remind, assure, convince, persuade. Flexible (both): warn, advise. Verbs with to + inf: ask, want, promise, hope, decide, offer. Verbs with object + to + inf: tell, ask, warn, advise, remind, want, allow, forbid, invite, order, persuade, encourage, expect. Verbs with -ing: suggest, admit, deny, confess, mention, recommend.

blocks.title: Reporting verbs: who takes what
blocks.rule: Reporting verbs vary in their patterns. Group 1: verb + that + clause. Say, think, believe, know, feel, hope, promise, admit, confess, agree, decide, declare, explain (+ to someone), insist, mention, remark, reply, state, suggest, warn (+ that). Group 2: verb + object + that + clause. Tell, inform, remind, assure, convince, persuade, warn. Group 3: verb + to + infinitive. Agree, ask, decide, hope, offer, promise, refuse, threaten, choose, want, demand. Group 4: verb + object + to + infinitive (reported requests, orders). Tell, ask, want, allow, forbid, invite, order, persuade, encourage, expect, warn, advise, remind. Group 5: verb + -ing. Suggest, admit, deny, confess, mention, recommend, propose. Note the fine difference: suggest + -ing (I suggest eating now) vs suggest + that + clause (I suggest that we eat now, with optional should). Admit, deny, confess accept both patterns (admit lying = admit that I lied). Explain uses «to» for the person (explain to me, not explain me).

sections.title: Christmas in Canada and the Italo-Canadian menu
sections.intro: Three pages: a Canadian Christmas calendar, the Italo-Canadian Vigilia, and multicultural December in Toronto.

blocks.text: In Canada Christmas opens with the [[Santa Claus Parade]] (Toronto's since 1905, mid-November), followed by weeks of lights (Yonge-Dundas Square, Casa Loma, the Cavalcade of Lights at Nathan Phillips Square), concerts (the Messiah by the TSO is sold out from October), markets (Christmas Market at the Distillery District, mid-November to late December), and skating (the City Hall rink opens the first week of December). [[Christmas Eve]] is a quiet family evening for Anglo-Canadian households and a loud multi-course dinner for Italo-Canadians. [[Christmas Day]] (statutory) is for presents, church (if attending), lunch and the Queen's Message replaced since 2022 by the King's. [[Boxing Day]] (statutory, 26 December) is the sales day — queues from 5 a.m. for electronics, especially after the pandemic turned it hybrid. [[New Year's Eve]] has fireworks on Lake Ontario and at Nathan Phillips Square. [[Jan 1]] is for a hangover; [[Jan 2]] (not a statutory holiday in Ontario) is back to work. One small language detail: [[Happy Holidays]] is the inclusive greeting in Canadian workplaces and schools; [[Merry Christmas]] is still used by many; [[Season's Greetings]] on cards; [[Boxing Day sale]] is universal.

The [[Vigilia]] of 24 December is the biggest meal of the Italo-Canadian year. The [[Feast of the Seven Fishes]] (le sette pietanze di pesce) is actually an [[Italo-American]] invention — probably Southern-Italian immigrants in New York, around 1900, elaborating a one-fish lenten tradition into a feast — that spread to Italo-Canada through family, migration and television. The usual seven: [[baccalà]] (salt cod, soaked), [[calamari]] (fried or in salad), [[sarde]] or [[alici]] (sardines, anchovies), [[scampi]] (shrimp, grilled or scampi-style), [[insalata di mare]] (cold seafood salad), a pasta ([[linguine con le vongole]] or [[spaghetti ai frutti di mare]]), and a big fish ([[orata]] or [[branzino]], whole, roasted). The dinner lasts four to five hours. Panettone, pandoro, [[struffoli]] (Neapolitan), [[cartellati]] (Puglian honey rings — like the ones Dora is making), [[cannoli]] (Sicilian), and espresso. The [[messa di mezzanotte]] follows for the devout. In Italy itself, the Vigilia is traditionally one fish dish (baccalà) and a lighter meal; the seven-fish spectacular is diaspora Italian. Chiara's first Vigilia in Toronto has twenty-two people around a table extended with sawhorses and planks.

blocks.title: Multicultural December
blocks.text: Toronto in December is also [[Hanukkah]] (the Jewish festival of lights, varies by lunar calendar, usually in December), [[Diwali]] (the Hindu festival of lights, late October or early November but the vibes last), [[Lunar New Year]] (late January or February, with the Chinatown parade), and smaller observances. Workplace parties default to [[Happy Holidays]] and gift exchanges to [[Secret Santa]] or [[White Elephant]] (an anonymous funny-gift swap) with a [[gift receipt]] (the receipt without the price so the recipient can return the gift). The [[Christmas card]] is sent in early December; the [[family newsletter]] inside the card is a WASP convention taken over by many immigrant families. The [[boxing week]] (26 December – 2 January) is Canada's statutory decompression. Chiara's experience of Toronto in December is Italo-Canadian in the house and multicultural outside it, which is Toronto exactly.

The three Italian Toronto neighbourhoods, in order of settlement. [[Little Italy]] on College Street from Bathurst to Ossington: the 1950s–1960s port of entry, now gentrifying, with a few remaining bakeries, cafés and the Italian Walk of Fame. [[Corso Italia]] on St Clair Avenue West from Dufferin to Caledonia: the 1960s–1980s hub for second-generation families moving north; still has the biggest Italian coffee bars and food shops. [[Woodbridge]] in Vaughan, 30 km north: the 1980s–2000s middle-class and third-generation suburb, with the biggest Italian population in Canada by proportion. Fourth and fifth generation now live anywhere in the GTA; the neighbourhoods are more culinary than demographic. [[Villa Charities]] at [[Columbus Centre]] (near Lawrence West station) is the civic home: elderly care, cultural programming, Italian school. The [[Italian Cultural Institute]] at the Consulate on St Clair runs lectures and screenings. All of these threads braid together on the Vigilia, and are the backdrop against which {hero} and Chiara eat their seven courses this year.
